description: 45 B2B company logos explained by a brand designer, from McKinsey, Accenture, and Deloitte to FedEx, Caterpillar, ServiceNow, and Deel.
intro:
B2B logos are judged by buyers who sign long contracts, so the best ones are credible enough for a procurement meeting and distinctive enough to be remembered after it.

What makes a good B2B logo?

Credibility: B2B brands sell to committees and procurement teams, so most use stable, confident wordmarks, like McKinsey, Deloitte, and Siemens.

One memorable detail: the best B2B logos add a single idea on top, like the hidden arrow in FedEx, the green dot in Deloitte, or the accent in Accenture.

Built to last: B2B logos live on trucks, machines, invoices, and contracts for decades, so they favor timeless shapes over trends.

Below are 45 B2B company logos in five groups, from enterprise software and consulting to logistics, industrial companies, and B2B platforms. Each one has a slide with my handwritten notes, followed by a short explanation. For software brands, see my reviews of SaaS logos and tech logos.

logoResearch.name: ServiceNow
logoResearch.verifiedFact: ServiceNow is an enterprise software company that automates IT and business workflows.
observations: The o in now is drawn as a green power button, a small detail that makes the name memorable.
A light, lowercase wordmark keeps an enterprise platform approachable.

logoResearch.name: Workday
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Workday is a cloud software company for HR and finance.
observations: An orange arc rises over the name like a sun, a hopeful image of the working day.
A friendly blue lowercase wordmark balances the warm arc.

logoResearch.name: Datadog
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Datadog is a cloud monitoring and security platform.
observations: A purple dog holding a chart is a playful mascot for a serious data product.
Spaced capitals under the mascot keep the stacked logo compact.

logoResearch.name: Autodesk
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Autodesk makes design and engineering software such as AutoCAD.
observations: A small, angled A mark sits beside a bold, all-caps wordmark.
Black and compact, the logo works across dozens of product brands.

logoResearch.name: Intuit
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Intuit is the company behind TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp.
observations: Wide, geometric blue capitals are built from simple lines and circles.
The parent brand stays simple so its product brands can lead.

logoResearch.name: Palantir
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Palantir builds data analytics software for governments and enterprises.
observations: A small ring on a stand looks like a seeing stone or a pin, a nod to the name from The Lord of the Rings.
A clean wordmark in black keeps the brand restrained.

logoResearch.name: Zoho
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Zoho is an Indian software company with a suite of business apps.
observations: Four overlapping squares in red, green, blue, and yellow form the letters of the name.
The tiny spaced ZOHO underneath works like a caption.

logoResearch.name: Box
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Box is a cloud content management company.
observations: Three heavy, rounded blue letters make one of the simplest logos in software.
The rounded b and o look like containers, matching the name.

logoResearch.name: Confluent
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Confluent is a data streaming company, now an IBM company.
observations: A burst of lines inside a circle shows data streams coming together.
Thin, spaced capitals feel precise and technical.

logoResearch.name: McKinsey & Company
logoResearch.verifiedFact: McKinsey & Company is a global management consulting firm.
observations: A serif wordmark on a navy block looks like a classic publication.
The ampersand ties the name together in a traditional, confident way.

logoResearch.name: Accenture
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Accenture is a global professional services and consulting company.
observations: A purple > accent sits over the t, the accent in Accenture and a symbol of looking forward.
A bold lowercase wordmark keeps the brand modern.

logoResearch.name: Deloitte
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Deloitte is one of the Big Four professional services firms.
observations: A bold black wordmark ends in a green dot, Deloitte's signature detail.
The green dot is so recognizable it works as a brand symbol on its own.

logoResearch.name: BCG
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Boston Consulting Group (BCG) is a global management consulting firm.
observations: Three huge, tight letters in deep green make one of the boldest consulting logos.
The overlapping C and G create a single, solid block.

logoResearch.name: Bain & Company
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Bain & Company is a global management consulting firm.
observations: Wide, spaced red capitals feel clean and confident.
A circle with an arrow at the end suggests direction and results.

logoResearch.name: PwC
logoResearch.verifiedFact: PwC is one of the Big Four professional services firms.
observations: A small, lowercase wordmark with an orange accent is far simpler than its old colorful logo.
Lowercase letters make a huge firm feel approachable.

logoResearch.name: EY
logoResearch.verifiedFact: EY is one of the Big Four professional services firms.
observations: A yellow beam above the letters looks like a ray of light or a rising line.
The tagline Shape the future with confidence sits beside the bold EY.

logoResearch.name: KPMG
logoResearch.verifiedFact: KPMG is one of the Big Four professional services firms.
observations: Four outlined boxes sit above the four letters, which stand for the firm's founders.
Italic blue capitals add movement.

logoResearch.name: Gartner
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Gartner is a research and advisory company.
observations: A bold navy wordmark with a small registered mark is the whole logo.
Rounded letters keep a research firm friendly.

logoResearch.name: FedEx
logoResearch.verifiedFact: FedEx is a global delivery and logistics company.
observations: A hidden arrow between the E and the x is one of the most famous negative-space tricks in design.
Purple and orange split Fed and Ex into two parts of one name.

logoResearch.name: UPS
logoResearch.verifiedFact: UPS is a global package delivery company.
observations: A brown shield with gold letters looks like a badge of reliability.
The curved top line of the shield suggests motion.

logoResearch.name: DHL
logoResearch.verifiedFact: DHL is a global logistics and express delivery company.
observations: Red italic letters on a yellow bar look fast, like a delivery truck passing by.
Speed lines on both sides extend the motion.

logoResearch.name: Maersk
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Maersk is a Danish shipping and logistics company.
observations: A white seven-pointed star on a light blue square is a symbol of guidance at sea.
Wide, spaced capitals feel steady and maritime.

logoResearch.name: Flexport
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Flexport is a technology-driven freight forwarding company.
observations: A heavy, rounded black wordmark with a custom f.
The lowercase letters make global logistics feel modern and simple.

logoResearch.name: C.H. Robinson
logoResearch.verifiedFact: C.H. Robinson is one of the world's largest logistics companies.
observations: A blue outlined hexagon looks like a 3D box or a network of routes.
Wide, spaced capitals feel institutional and steady.

logoResearch.name: Samsara
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Samsara makes connected operations software and sensors for fleets.
observations: A black, bird-like mark looks like a hawk or a guardian watching over operations.
Heavy, wide capitals make the brand bold.

logoResearch.name: project44
logoResearch.verifiedFact: project44 is a supply chain visibility platform.
observations: A blue circle holds the number 44, like a stamp or a tracking badge.
Condensed blue lowercase letters keep the long name compact.

logoResearch.name: Uber Freight
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Uber Freight is a logistics and freight brokerage company.
observations: A thin, clean wordmark extends the Uber brand into logistics.
With no symbol, the familiar name carries the brand.

logoResearch.name: Caterpillar
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Caterpillar is the world's largest maker of construction and mining equipment.
observations: A yellow triangle under the A looks like a pile of earth or a construction ramp.
Heavy, condensed black capitals feel as tough as the machines.

logoResearch.name: 3M
logoResearch.verifiedFact: 3M is a global manufacturer of industrial, safety, and consumer products.
observations: Two heavy red characters make one of the shortest logos in business.
The tight, bold shapes feel solid and confident.

logoResearch.name: Honeywell
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Honeywell is an industrial technology conglomerate.
observations: A red H mark sits next to a two-line red wordmark.
The bold, compact letters feel engineered.

logoResearch.name: Siemens
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Siemens is a German industrial technology company.
observations: Wide, teal capitals are the whole logo, unchanged for decades.
The petrol color is one of the most recognizable in industry.

logoResearch.name: Schneider Electric
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Schneider Electric is a French energy management and automation company.
observations: A green circle with a stylized S and E marks the electric side of the name.
The grey, two-line wordmark feels technical and calm.

logoResearch.name: ABB
logoResearch.verifiedFact: ABB is a Swiss-Swedish electrification and automation company.
observations: Three red letters are cut by white horizontal lines, like an electrical grid.
The striped letters make a short name distinctive.

logoResearch.name: Bosch
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Bosch is a German engineering and technology company.
observations: The symbol is a stylized magneto armature, a part from Bosch's early ignition systems.
Bold red capitals carry the name.

logoResearch.name: John Deere
logoResearch.verifiedFact: John Deere is a US maker of agricultural and construction machinery.
observations: A leaping deer inside a green shape is one of the most famous symbols in farming.
Green and yellow are so tied to the brand that they are protected colors.

logoResearch.name: Dow
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Dow is a global materials science company.
observations: A red diamond holds the name, a shape Dow has used for over a century.
The white letters inside the diamond read clearly at any size.

logoResearch.name: Deel
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Deel is a global payroll and HR platform for remote teams.
observations: A heavy lowercase wordmark ends with a period, like a confident statement.
The short name and dot keep the brand simple and memorable.

logoResearch.name: Toast
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Toast is a point-of-sale and software platform for restaurants.
observations: A slice of toast drawn as a simple outline is a literal, friendly symbol.
A rounded orange wordmark feels warm, like a restaurant.

logoResearch.name: Procore
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Procore is a construction management software company.
observations: Heavy black capitals with a custom O and R feel like construction signage.
The bold letters suit a product used on job sites.

logoResearch.name: ZoomInfo
logoResearch.verifiedFact: ZoomInfo is a B2B data and go-to-market platform.
observations: A red square with a Z is an app-icon-like symbol.
A light lowercase wordmark keeps the brand friendly.

logoResearch.name: Faire
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Faire is an online wholesale marketplace for independent retailers.
observations: Widely spaced serif capitals look like a boutique or fashion brand.
The light, elegant type fits a marketplace for independent shops.

logoResearch.name: Alibaba
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Alibaba is a Chinese e-commerce and B2B marketplace company.
observations: A bold orange wordmark with a rounded, friendly feel.
Alibaba is one of the world's largest B2B trading platforms.

logoResearch.name: Grainger
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Grainger is a US distributor of industrial supplies.
observations: Heavy italic black capitals look strong and fast.
Red stripes underneath add speed and an industrial accent.

logoResearch.name: Uline
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Uline is a US distributor of shipping and packaging supplies.
observations: Bold white capitals on a navy block look like a label on a box.
The simple block shape is easy to print on catalogs and boxes.

logoResearch.name: Coupa
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Coupa is a business spend management platform.
observations: A burst-like flower mark suggests growth and connections.
A heavy lowercase wordmark feels confident.

listIntro: The boards below show all 45 B2B logos in one consistent format, grouped into enterprise software, consulting, logistics, industrial, and B2B platforms.
Each logo is reviewed for its design decisions, not for the company's size or services.
sectionIntroductions: Enterprise software brands sell to IT and finance teams, so their logos balance friendly lowercase type with a clean, reliable feel.
Consulting firms sell expertise and trust, and their logos lean on bold, confident wordmarks with one signature detail.
Logistics brands live on trucks, planes, and boxes, so their logos are bold, colorful, and readable from far away.
Industrial companies have some of the oldest and most consistent logos in business, built to work on machines and products for decades.
Newer B2B platforms look more like consumer apps, with friendly marks and simple, modern type.
sectionBridge: This is a visual comparison of B2B company logos, not a ranking of companies.
Look at how each logo balances credibility with one memorable detail.
entryFallbacks: The identity relies on a few clear decisions to stay recognizable.
Notice how the logo would look on a contract, a truck, or a trade show booth.

findings.heading: One small detail makes a B2B logo memorable
findings.text: The FedEx arrow, the Deloitte dot, the Accenture accent, and the ServiceNow power button show how one small idea makes a plain wordmark unforgettable.

findings.heading: Industrial logos are built to last
findings.text: Siemens, Bosch, John Deere, and Dow have kept the same core logo for decades, proof that consistency builds recognition in B2B.

findings.heading: Consulting is going bold and simple
findings.text: BCG, PwC, and EY have moved to bolder, simpler logos with one accent color to stand out in a conservative category.

findings.heading: Modern B2B looks like consumer tech
findings.text: Deel, Toast, Flexport, and Zoho use friendly, rounded logos that would fit a consumer app.

logoRosterConfig.checklistHeading: A practical checklist for a new B2B logo
checklistItems: Does the logo look credible in a procurement meeting and on a contract?
Is there one memorable detail, not a pile of ideas?
Will it work on vehicles, products, invoices, and a website for decades?
Does it still read when printed small and in one color?
Is it distinctive from competitors in your industry, not just from other B2B brands?

faq.question: What makes a good B2B logo?
faq.answer: A good B2B logo looks credible to buyers, works across vehicles, products, documents, and screens, and adds one memorable detail. Examples like FedEx, Deloitte, and Accenture combine a stable wordmark with a single idea, like a hidden arrow, a green dot, or an accent mark.

faq.question: How are B2B logos different from B2C logos?
faq.answer: B2B logos usually aim for credibility and longevity rather than excitement, because they sell to committees and sign long contracts. They tend to use stable wordmarks and restrained color, while B2C logos are often more playful and trend-driven.

faq.question: What is the hidden arrow in the FedEx logo?
faq.answer: The FedEx logo hides an arrow in the negative space between the E and the x. It suggests speed and forward movement, and it is one of the most famous examples of negative space in logo design.
